slides.title: Alibaba Launches Qwen-Robot Series Embodied AI Large Models
slides.tldr: ALIBABA RELEASES QWEN-ROBOT EMBODIED AI MODELS
slides.highlight: The launch of the Qwen-Robot series of embodied AI large models is relevant to RwB's focus on embodied social robots and AI-mediated learning.

slides.title: MuVAP: Multimodal Multiparty Voice Activity Projection for Turn-taking Prediction in the Wild
slides.highlight: MuVAP utilizes a causal multimodal framework to enable speaker-aware turn-taking predictions from a single camera and monaural audio, supporting HyECHO's focus on multimodal social perception and listener modeling.

card.one_liner: MuVAP predicts turn-taking in multiparty conversations using a single camera and monaural audio stream.
card.key_idea: A causal multimodal framework using Role-Relative Projection to map N-speaker dynamics onto a fixed current-versus-next floor-holder state, grounding acoustic predictions in face tracks.
card.evaluation: Evaluated on the new 31-hour AVCC dataset using Shift-Hold (Macro-F1) and Next Speaker Prediction (Accuracy) tasks; outperformed MLP and unimodal baselines.
card.limitation: Performance is lower in active prediction tasks compared to silent ones and decreases as the number of speakers increases.

slides.title: Evaluating Large Language Models Abilities for Addressee, Turn-change, and Next Speaker Prediction in Meetings
slides.highlight: This research evaluates LLMs and multimodal LLMs on addressee detection and speaker prediction, contributing to HyECHO's focus on addressee/listener modeling and engagement in hybrid teams.

card.one_liner: LLMs outperform humans and supervised models in next speaker prediction for multi-party meetings using conversational context.
card.key_idea: A unified framework evaluating addressee detection, turn-change, and next speaker prediction across supervised models, text-based LLMs, and multimodal LLMs (MM-LLMs).
card.evaluation: Evaluated on the AMI Meeting Corpus using accuracy and F1 scores, comparing models against human subjects in online multimodal settings.
card.limitation: MM-LLMs struggle to effectively leverage raw audio-visual signals; human evaluations were conducted by non-native English speakers.

slides.title: Beyond Usability: A UX Case Study on Using "Withdrawal Design" to Challenge Engagement Metrics in Social Robotics
slides.tldr: CHALLENGING ENGAGEMENT METRICS IN SOCIAL ROBOTICS
slides.highlight: This study examines how the removal of a social robot can prompt children with autism to seek human interaction, suggesting that high engagement may sometimes silo social behavior. It is relevant to RwB's focus on human-robot interaction and embodied social robots.

card.one_liner: Withdrawal of social robots may better promote human social interaction than continuous robot engagement.
card.key_idea: A mixed-methods RCT comparing children who kept a social robot versus those who had it withdrawn to evaluate long-term social outcomes.
card.evaluation: 8-week home RCT (N=40) using SCARED, RCADS, SMS, RMET, and SUS metrics; results show a trade-off between anxiety and social motivation.

slides.title: Generating Natural and Expressive Robot Gestures through Iterative Reinforcement Learning with Human Feedback using LLMs
slides.tldr: RLHF-TUNED LLM GESTURE GENERATION FOR HUMANOID ROBOTS
slides.highlight: This research uses RLHF and LLMs to generate more expressive and fluid co-speech gestures for the Pepper humanoid robot, contributing to the development of embodied social robots in RwB.

card.one_liner: Iterative RLHF improves the expressiveness, relevance, and fluidity of LLM-generated co-speech gestures for humanoid robots.
card.key_idea: GPT-4 generates gesture code using low-level motion primitives, refined through five iterations of offline Direct Preference Optimization (DPO) and online few-shot prompting based on human ratings.
card.evaluation: 250 participants rated 20 videos per iteration on a 5-point Likert scale. Results showed statistically significant improvements (p<0.001) by the final iteration.
card.limitation: Relying on low-level primitives can lead to mode collapse, repetitive patterns, and difficulty sustaining gesture diversity.

slides.title: SkillMoV: Mixture-of-View Routing with Prototype-Conditioned Gating for Unified Multi-View Proficiency Estimation
slides.highlight: SkillMoV utilizes a Mixture-of-View Projector to estimate human proficiency from synchronized ego and exo-view videos, aligning with MOSAIC's focus on multi-view proficiency estimation.

card.one_liner: SkillMoV improves multi-view human proficiency estimation using a view-conditioned mixture-of-experts routing framework.
card.key_idea: A Mixture-of-View Projector (MoVP) uses soft routing across expert MLPs, cross-view attention, prototype anchoring, and gated projection to adapt to heterogeneous camera viewpoints.
card.evaluation: Evaluated on EgoExo4D across six domains; achieved 50.17% accuracy in Exos setting, surpassing the strongest baseline by 3.57 percentage points.
card.limitation: Performance is lower in Ego-only settings (40.00%) and prototypes lack direct interpretability as calibrated ordinal class representatives.

slides.title: A Causal Model of Theory of Mind in Conflict for Artificial Intelligence
slides.tldr: CAUSAL MODEL FOR SELECTIVE THEORY OF MIND ENGAGEMENT
slides.highlight: This research proposes a structural causal model to determine when AI should engage Theory of Mind, supporting ADAM-CHAT's goal of inferring partner intent via theory of mind.

card.one_liner: A structural causal model determining when AI should engage Theory of Mind (ToM) during conflict.
card.key_idea: A DAG-based framework treating ToM as a resource-rational mechanism triggered by information asymmetry, low solution tractability, and perceived sophistication mismatches to optimize epistemic accuracy.
card.evaluation: Not clearly stated; the paper provides a theoretical framework and structural equations, noting that simulation and empirical validation are goals for future work.
card.limitation: The model is currently static and dyadic, with several functional forms and the 'intuitive mode' left unspecified for future empirical calibration.

slides.title: WaveSync: Constrained Wavefront Optimization for Synchronized Co-Speech Gestures in Humanoid Robots
slides.highlight: WaveSync uses a hybrid framework to align expressive gestures with speech emphasis while ensuring kinematic feasibility on physical humanoid robots. This is relevant to RwB's focus on embodied social robots and human-robot interaction.

card.one_liner: WaveSync synchronizes humanoid robot gestures with speech emphasis while respecting strict kinematic and dynamic hardware constraints.
card.key_idea: An LLM generates a Semantic Importance Wave; Dynamic Movement Primitives shape trajectories, and a Wavefront Optimizer aligns gesture peaks to speech peaks via duration compression and forward propagation.
card.evaluation: Evaluated in PyBullet across five dialogue scenarios using objective metrics (HbS, PAM, Jerk) and subjective Likert ratings from 20 participants; outperformed three ablated baselines.
card.limitation: Relies on a fixed action library, which limits the system's ability to handle unconstrained dialogue.

slides.title: Fast When, Careful Who: Dual-Process Multiparty Turn-Taking with Diffusion Augmentation
slides.highlight: This work proposes a two-stage audio-only pipeline for multiparty turn-taking that separates turn boundary triggering from floor transfer verification, supporting HyECHO's focus on diarization and listener modeling.

card.one_liner: A dual-process audio pipeline for multiparty turn-taking using diffusion-based background augmentation to improve shift detection.
card.key_idea: A fast WavLM-based 'gate' proposes turn boundaries, while a slow ECAPA-TDNN 'verifier' confirms floor transfers (HOLD/SHIFT) and predicts the next speaker.
card.evaluation: Evaluated on VoxConverse using precision, recall, F1, and MAE; compared against a ResCNN-Siamese baseline and Voice Activity Projection (VAP).
card.limitation: Performance is constrained by boundary coverage, particularly in heavily overlapped or fast-exchange regions where acoustic cues are ambiguous.

slides.title: Co-Creating Buildable and Open Social Robot Study Companions with University Students
slides.highlight: This research demonstrates how Design for Assembly and Disassembly can lower barriers for students building social robots, which is relevant to RwB's focus on embodied social robots and human-robot interaction.

card.one_liner: DfA and DfD mechanical redesigns significantly improve the usability and perceived buildability of open-source social robots.
card.key_idea: Applied the Double Diamond framework to redesign the Robot Study Companion (RSC v4.1) using twist-lock fasteners, snap-fit joints, and tool-free service latches to reduce assembly friction.
card.evaluation: Two studies with developers and first-time builders using SUS, NASA-TLX, and assembly timing; SUS rose from 59.4 to 89.4 for developers.
card.limitation: Small, non-random samples and a lack of inter-rater reliability checks for thematic coding.

slides.title: Tuning Agent-Based Predator-Prey Models Toward Lotka-Volterra Dynamics
slides.tldr: TUNING AGENT-BASED MODELS FOR STABLE POPULATION DYNAMICS
slides.highlight: This research explores tuning parameters in agent-based models with neural network controllers to achieve stable population oscillations, supporting MIMIC's focus on meso-scale simulation and agent-based modeling.

card.one_liner: Tuning agent-based predator-prey models using a feature-based loss to achieve stable Lotka-Volterra population oscillations.
card.key_idea: Uses CMA-ES to optimize ecological parameters (energy, birth/death thresholds) via a loss function rewarding lagged population correlations, persistence, and bounded oscillations in a JAX-based ABM.
card.evaluation: Evaluated using random and evolved CTRNN controllers; results show successful emergence of oscillatory dynamics and spatial organization, with evolved agents providing more bounded trajectories.
card.limitation: The loss function is indirect and hand-designed, rather than derived from a direct mathematical trajectory match.

slides.title: Self-Driving Negotiator: An interactive, verifiable benchmark for social negotiation and theory of mind under hidden intent
slides.tldr: BENCHMARK FOR SOCIAL NEGOTIATION IN DRIVING
slides.highlight: This work introduces a benchmark for measuring implicit social coordination and the inference of hidden intent, supporting ADAM-CHAT's focus on theory of mind and adaptive human-AI teaming.

card.one_liner: A text-based interactive benchmark measuring LLMs' ability to infer hidden driver intent through social negotiation.
card.key_idea: A multi-turn POMDP environment where agents must deduce latent dispositions (e.g., committed vs. yielding) from behavioral cues to coordinate safely without explicit communication.
card.evaluation: Six LLMs were tested across three scenarios (yield, pedestrian, merge) using success rates and decision-correctness; results show models trail a scripted expert.
card.limitation: The benchmark is text-only, deliberately omitting perception and visual processing to isolate social reasoning from sensor-based noise.

slides.title: Multimodal Physiological Assessment of Contact-Rich Physical Human-Robot Interaction Under Varying Environmental Conditions
slides.tldr: PHYSIOLOGICAL IMPACT OF ENVIRONMENTAL STRESSORS ON pHRI
slides.highlight: This study identifies hidden physiological costs in contact-rich human-robot interaction, supporting RwB's focus on human-robot interaction by suggesting physiology-aware control to reduce operator workload.

card.one_liner: Task performance in contact-rich pHRI remains stable despite environmental stressors, though autonomic workload increases with temperature.
card.key_idea: A multimodal study using sEMG, EDA, and eye-tracking to decompose operator workload into physical, cognitive, and autonomic dimensions during robot-assisted tracing tasks under varying environmental conditions.
card.evaluation: 12 participants performed tracing tasks across 18 combinations of temperature, noise, and illuminance; results analyzed via ANOVA, t-tests, and Spearman correlations.
card.limitation: Participant pool lacked industrial pHRI experience and environmental conditions were controlled rather than dynamic/unpredictable.

slides.title: Two pizzas and a prototype: How agentic AI is rewiring Amazon’s teams and upending its traditions
slides.highlight: The use of agentic AI to restructure team dynamics is relevant to ADAM-CHAT's focus on adaptive AI teammates for human-AI teaming.

slides.title: Click4Assistance Launches FIFA World Cup 2026 AI Agent Experience
slides.highlight: The launch of an AI agent experience for fan engagement relates to HyECHO's focus on multimodal social perception and engagement within human-AI teams.

slides.title: LOPAL: Local Performance-Aware Active Learning from Imperfect Demonstrations
slides.highlight: LOPAL improves robot skill acquisition by using local quality assessments of human demonstrations and active data acquisition via shared autonomy. This relates to MOSAIC's focus on estimating human proficiency and adaptive AI coaching to improve skill acquisition.

card.one_liner: LOPAL improves robot skill acquisition by leveraging local performance variations within imperfect human demonstrations.
card.key_idea: A GMM encodes trajectories and local quality; Gaussian Mixture Regression then generates motions targeting high-performance regions, supplemented by interpolation and shared-autonomy active data acquisition.
card.evaluation: Validated via 2D car driving simulation and a real-world pipe inspection task; showed up to 27.31% performance improvement over baselines.

slides.title: Whole-Body Impedance Model Predictive Control for Safe Physical Human--Robot Interaction on Floating-Base Platforms
slides.highlight: This work proposes a three-level architecture for floating-base robots to maintain balance while interacting safely with humans. It is relevant to RwB for enhancing the safety and stability of embodied social robots during physical human-robot interaction.

card.one_liner: A three-level MPC framework for floating-base robots to achieve zero steady-state error during human-robot interaction.
card.key_idea: Combines centroidal MPC for balance, a priority-driven WBC layer, and a Kalman-augmented Impedance MPC using contact-consistent mass inverses to reject pHRI disturbances.
card.evaluation: Simulated on a 17-DOF biped and Unitree G1 in MuJoCo; compared against PD/PI and fixed-base MPC, achieving sub-0.05mm steady-state error.
card.limitation: Stability and zero steady-state error are only guaranteed within singularity-free workspaces where the platform maintains a valid support polygon.

slides.title: Correct Yourself, Keep My Trust: How Self-Correction and Social Connection Shape Credibility in Social Chatbots
slides.highlight: This research demonstrates that self-correction maintains trustworthiness and expertise more effectively than external corrections, aligning with ADAM-CHAT's focus on self-monitoring and self-correction for human-AI teaming.

card.one_liner: Self-correction preserves a social chatbot's credibility and leverages social bonds to improve error correction effectiveness.
card.key_idea: Comparing self-correction against external sources (webpage, expert chatbot), the study found self-correction maintains trustworthiness and expertise while utilizing social attraction and self-disclosure to amplify belief change.
card.evaluation: Between-subjects experiment (N=120) using 7-point Likert scales, ANOVAs, and OLS regression. Results showed significant credibility gains for self-correction over external sources.

slides.title: Improving Medical Communication using Rubric-Guided Counterfactual Recommendations
slides.highlight: This research introduces an LM-guided pipeline to refine communication features in patient-doctor interactions, supporting MIMIC's focus on LLM-based agent models for societal-scale impact analysis.

card.one_liner: An LM-guided pipeline that recommends minimal, interpretable communication changes to increase positive patient feedback in telemedicine.
card.key_idea: Uses APO for feature discovery and refinement, trains a CatBoost policy model for feedback prediction, and searches for budget-constrained counterfactual feature modifications.
card.evaluation: Evaluated via temporal holdout using independent auditor models (LR, EBM); achieved 71.5% ROC-AUC and +6.41% mean gain in predicted positive feedback.
card.limitation: Evaluation was conducted offline; the system requires prospective real-world validation to measure actual impact on patient feedback.

slides.title: Large Language Models as Supervised Extraction Assistants: Lowering the Barrier to Documentation Standard Adoption in Agent-Based Modelling
slides.highlight: This research explores using LLMs to automate the extraction of documentation standards for Agent-Based Modelling, supporting the development of transparent agent models for MIMIC.

card.one_liner: LLMs can reduce the effort of adopting ABM documentation standards through human-supervised data extraction.
card.key_idea: A 'supervised extraction' workflow where LLMs draft reports based on standards (e.g., RAT-RS) and humans act as reviewers, shifting the researcher's role from producer to critic.
card.evaluation: Feasibility study using four LLMs on one ABM paper; evaluated via cosine similarity against human benchmarks and intra-model consistency across repeated runs.
card.limitation: Performance is less reliable for explanatory and evaluative tasks compared to factual/descriptive ones; results lack statistical generalizability due to the single-paper sample.

slides.title: Reference-Driven Multi-Speaker Audio Scene Generation from In-the-Wild Priors
slides.highlight: ScenA generates multi-speaker audio scenes with overlapping dialogue and ambient noise, contributing to HyECHO's goals of multimodal social perception and diarization.

card.one_liner: ScenA generates multi-speaker audio scenes from natural language prompts and reference voices without structured supervision.
card.key_idea: A flow-matching model using latent concatenation and identity-aware positional encodings, employing a high-noise-biased timestep distribution to prevent the model from bypassing text prompts via acoustic similarity.
card.evaluation: Evaluated on CoVoMix2-Dialogue benchmarks using WER, cpSIM, and ACC; outperformed multi-speaker baselines in speaker-binding and human preference tests.
card.limitation: Limited to 20-second generation duration and a maximum of three reference speakers.
